decision.summaryForCoordinator: The quotation discipline holds. The subject's fcConsentExactByteIntent is a character-for-character match to live doctor-contract.v4's FC-CONSENT exactByteIntent, and all seven verbatimFromV4 strings were tested as substrings of that live text rather than read: all seven present. The composition is four plus three — one invocation per action class with consent named, each of CA-1 through CA-4 appearing exactly once, plus denied-by-policy, non-interactive-no-policy and networked-target-without-CA-4. CA-1 through CA-4 are the live consentableActionClasses in v4, and keeping them as four separate states with four separate consents is what v4's consentDoesNotCascade rule requires. The one structured claim that goes beyond its quoted phrase — actionClass 'not-CA-4' on the networked-target state — was traced to v4's own failsIf entry 'a networked-posture target is executed under CA-1/CA-2 alone', which licenses it; where v4 is genuinely silent the subject records 'not-selected-here' instead. Nothing prohibited is authored: consentRecordBytes and observations are both the bare token NOT-AUTHORED, no CA behaviour or check id appears, and the states carry no path, digest or tree structure. The remaining-class arithmetic is right at ten of twelve. Custody is clean: subject unmoved at ccacc54a and 0444, six of six cited digests equal live bytes including the two sibling corpora this reviewer ACCEPTed in the preceding cycles, file 08 pin equal to live and unmodified, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, and neither QUALIFIED nor SATISFIED occurs anywhere. Fifteen attacks run, fifteen refuted, zero findings. One repeat observation: this is the second consecutive doctor input corpus to cite the superseded G12 v2 with its ACCEPT annotation while the chain's head, v3, carries a REJECT. Nothing technical turns on it since the two versions' retainedEvidence is byte-identical, but if further corpora follow the template the pattern will propagate, and settling the referent once would fix it for the series.
